models.inverse_notes: Solve d_o given f,d_i: d_o=f*d_i/(d_i-f); require f!=0,d_i!=0,d_i!=f and reconstructed d_o>0, then all original forward guards. Solve f given d_o,d_i: f=d_o*d_i/(d_o+d_i); require d_o>0,d_i!=0,d_o+d_i!=0; resulting f finite/nonzero. Unique roots in either direction. Check f=0.1,d_i=0.125 -> d_o=0.5 and 1/0.5+1/0.125=10=1/f. Virtual case d_o=0.05,d_i=-0.1 -> f=0.1. d_i=f requires object at infinity, outside finite inputs. d_i=-d_o corresponds to zero optical power/infinite f, not f=0. At d_o=f the physically meaningful collimated limit is excluded only from this finite-output serialization.
limitations: No finite image distance exists when d_o=f: the output beam is collimated, rather than physically impossible.
Finite-scalar model excludes object at infinity and zero-power optical elements with infinite focal length.
Aberrations, diffraction and thick-lens principal planes require other descriptions; this relation alone does not locate lens surfaces.

references.method: Published Example 2.4(a): preserve reported 12.5 cm as expected 0.125 m. A 0.0005 m tolerance is half of its 0.1 cm reporting increment; inputs are the textbook nominal values, not measured uncertainty bounds.
Published Example 2.4(b): preserve -10.0 cm as -0.100 m; tolerance half of its last reported 0.1 cm increment. This changes image sign and is not a zero boundary.

Independent geometric construction with a synthetic 0.010 m object. The undeviated center ray has height y=-x/60; the incident-parallel ray emerges with y=0.010+x/20, extending back to focus -0.2 m. Intersect: -x/60=0.010+x/20, giving x=-0.15 m. This uses two ray rules, not reevaluation of the serialized rational expression. Tolerance covers binary arithmetic on these exact synthetic values.

rejection_cases.reason: Object at focal point gives parallel output rays; the finite image-distance denominator vanishes.
Zero focal length was excluded in the original reciprocal equation and cannot be restored by algebraic simplification.
Object at the reference plane is not a finite conjugate under the original reciprocal equation.

models.summary: One canonical finite-conjugate imaging law under a real-is-positive convention; focal length includes either sign and the image may be real or virtual. Real objects are the directly evidenced application profile.
models.title: Thin-lens and paraxial spherical-mirror imaging

variables.context: Same paraxial homogeneous thin lens, ordered incident and exit surfaces, common homogeneous exterior medium on both sides, wavelength and material state. Real-is-positive focal convention: positive converging, negative diverging. Positive signed surface curvature has its center on the outgoing side; first biconvex curvature positive and second negative.
variables.definition: Signed paraxial focal distance of the selected optical element in its supplied exterior medium and wavelength conditions.
variables.domain: Finite nonzero; positive for a converging lens/concave mirror and negative for a diverging lens/convex mirror.

variables.context: Same paraxial thin lens (center reference, same exterior medium on both sides) or spherical mirror (vertex reference), optical axis, real object and wavelength/medium conditions. Real-is-positive convention: d_o>0, d_i>0 for real images and d_i<0 for virtual images; f>0 converging lens/concave mirror, f<0 diverging lens/convex mirror.
variables.definition: Real-is-positive axial distance from lens center or mirror vertex to the real object.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive real-object profile; d_o=f excluded in the forward finite-image view.
